lesson_scope: Connected particle systems consisting of a particle on a horizontal or inclined plane connected via a light inextensible string over a smooth pulley to a hanging mass; uniform tension across smooth pulleys; resultant force on pulley axle (magnitude and direction); limiting equilibrium under Coulomb friction; and external horizontal or angled stabilizing forces.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 1: Horizontal rough table with hanging mass

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Horizontal rough table with hanging mass

hints: The normal reaction on the table is $R_A = 6(10) = 60\text{ N}$, so maximum friction is $F_{\max} = 0.35(60) = 21\text{ N}$.
In equilibrium, the string tension balances both friction and the hanging weight: $T = F_{\max} = 21\text{ N} \implies m(10) = 21 \implies m = 2.1\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate normal reaction and maximum static friction on block $A$:
$$R_A = m_A g = 6(10) = 60\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\max} = \mu R_A = 0.35(60) = 21\text{ N}$$

Equate the maximum holding tension to the weight of hanging mass $m$:
$$T_{\max} = F_{\max} = 21\text{ N}$$
$$m g = 21 \implies m = \frac{21}{10} = 2.1\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compute table grip:
- Normal force is $60\text{ N}$:
$$F_{\max} = 0.35 \times 60 = 21\text{ N}$$

Find maximum suspended weight:
- The rope can support up to $21\text{ N}$ before slipping:
$$m = \frac{21}{10} = 2.1\text{ kg}$$
Any mass up to $2.1\text{ kg}$ remains stationary.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates normal reaction $R_A = 60\text{ N}$ and maximum friction $F_{\max} = 0.35(60) = 21\text{ N}$.
Equates string tension $T = 21\text{ N}$ to hanging weight $mg$ to find $m = 2.1\text{ kg}$.

$$T = 3 \times 10 = 30\text{ N}$$

Combine perpendicular forces:
- The pulley feels $30\text{ N}$ horizontally and $30\text{ N}$ vertically:
$$R_P = \sqrt{30^2 + 30^2} = 30\sqrt{2} \approx 42.4\text{ N}$$
The resultant acts at $45^\circ$ below the horizontal.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Smooth incline connected to hanging mass in equilibrium

$$\Sigma F_\perp = R_A - m_A g\cos 30^\circ = 0$$
$$R_A = 50\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3013 \approx 43.3\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Balance along the smooth slope:
- Downhill weight is $25\text{ N}$, so tension is $25\text{ N}$:
$$m_B = \frac{25}{10} = 2.5\text{ kg}$$

Find normal reaction:
$$R_A = 50\cos 30^\circ = 25\sqrt{3} \approx 43.3\text{ N}$$
The slope supports $43.3\text{ N}$ perpendicular to the surface.

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 4: Pulley reaction force at the crest of an inclined plane

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 4: Pulley reaction force at the crest of an inclined plane

hints: The string segment along the plane is inclined at $30^\circ$ above the horizontal. The hanging segment is vertical ($90^\circ$ below horizontal). The angle between the two tension vectors is $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$.
Use the formula for two equal forces of magnitude $T$ separated by angle $\theta = 60^\circ$: $R_P = 2T\cos(60^\circ / 2) = 2(40)\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.3\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Determine the angle $\theta$ between the two string segments:
- The segment to the slope points down the incline at $30^\circ$ below the horizontal.
- The segment to the hanging mass points vertically downwards ($90^\circ$ below the horizontal).
- The angle between them is:
$$\theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force on the pulley:
$$R_P = 2T\cos\left(\frac{\theta}{2}\right) = 2(40)\cos 30^\circ = 80\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.2820 \approx 69.3\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the string angle at the crest:
- The slope segment is $30^\circ$ from horizontal, and the hanging segment is vertical ($90^\circ$):
$$\theta = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$$

Apply the symmetric resultant formula:
- Two $40\text{ N}$ tensions at $60^\circ$ combine along their angle bisector:
$$R_P = 2 \times 40\cos 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3} \approx 69.3\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies angle between string segments as $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$ (or uses components $X = 40\cos 30^\circ, Y = 40 + 40\sin 30^\circ$).

questions.difficulty_reason: Foundational Drill: Drill 5: Rough incline with hanging mass on verge of descending

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 5: Rough incline with hanging mass on verge of descending

hints: Because block $A$ is on the verge of sliding up the slope, friction acts down the slope.

Normal reaction is $R_A = 40\cos 30^\circ = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$, so friction is $F_{\max} = 0.25(20\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$. Equilibrium along the slope gives $T = 40\sin 30^\circ + 5\sqrt{3} = 28.66\text{ N} \implies m_B = 2.87\text{ kg}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate normal reaction and maximum static friction on block $A$:
$$R_A = m_A g\cos 30^\circ = 4(10)\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 20\sqrt{3} \approx 34.6410\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\max} = \mu R_A = 0.25(20\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.6603\text{ N}$$

Set up equilibrium along the slope with friction acting down:
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = T - m_A g\sin 30^\circ - F_{\max} = 0$$
$$T = 40(0.5) + 5\sqrt{3} = 20 + 8.6603 = 28.6603\text{ N}$$
$$m_B = \frac{T}{g} = \frac{28.6603}{10} \approx 2.8660 \approx 2.87\text{ kg}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Determine downhill resistance forces:
- Downhill weight is $20\text{ N}$.
- Downhill friction grip is:
$$F_{\max} = 0.25 \times 20\sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$$

Find required counterweight:
- The tension must overcome both forces:
$$T = 20 + 8.66 = 28.66\text{ N} \implies m_B = 2.87\text{ kg}$$
A hanging mass of $2.87\text{ kg}$ puts the block on the verge of sliding upward.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates $R_A = 40\cos 30^\circ = 20\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ and $F_{\max} = 0.25(20\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$ acting down the slope.

$$4(3 + m_\text{add}) = 25 \implies m_\text{add} = 3.25\text{ kg}$$
Adding $3.25\text{ kg}$ on top stops the block from sliding.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 2: Particle on rough slope with hanging mass

hints: Downhill weight is $50\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$ and uphill tension is $20\text{ N}$. The downhill pull dominates, so friction acts up the slope.

Required friction is $F_f = 25 - 20 = 5\text{ N}$ up the slope. Compare with maximum friction $F_{\max} = 0.2(25\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$. Since $5\text{ N} < 8.66\text{ N}$, the particle stays at rest.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve along the line of greatest slope to find the required balancing friction force:
- Downhill weight: $W_\parallel = 50\sin 30^\circ = 25\text{ N}$.
- Uphill tension: $T = 20\text{ N}$.
Because downhill weight exceeds tension, the particle tends to slip down, so friction acts up the slope:
$$F_f = W_\parallel - T = 25 - 20 = 5\text{ N} \quad (\text{acting up the slope})$$

Verify against the maximum static friction threshold:
$$F_{\max} = \mu R_A = 0.2(25\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.6603\text{ N}$$
Since $F_f = 5\text{ N} \leqslant F_{\max} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$, the static friction requirement is comfortably met and equilibrium is confirmed:
$$F_f = 5\text{ N} \quad (\text{up the slope})$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Compare slope forces:
- Downhill weight pull is $25\text{ N}$.
- Uphill rope tension is $20\text{ N}$:
$$W_\parallel - T = 25 - 20 = 5\text{ N} \quad (\text{downhill imbalance})$$
Friction must provide $5\text{ N}$ pointing uphill to restore balance.

Check friction capacity:
$$F_{\max} = 0.2 \times 25\sqrt{3} = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$$
Since $5\text{ N} < 8.66\text{ N}$, the particle does not budge.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves along the slope: $F_f = 50\sin 30^\circ - 20 = 5\text{ N}$ directed up the slope.
Confirms equilibrium by showing $F_f = 5\text{ N} < F_{\max} = 0.2(25\sqrt{3}) = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ N}$.

Resolve the tension forces exerted by the two string segments on the pulley along horizontal and vertical axes:
- Horizontal component (from inclined string segment):
$$X = T\cos\alpha = 32(0.8) = 25.6\text{ N} \quad (\text{towards the slope})$$

- Inclined segment pulls downwards with $T\sin\alpha = 32(0.6) = 19.2\text{ N}$.
- Vertical hanging segment pulls downwards with $T = 32\text{ N}$:
$$Y = T + T\sin\alpha = 32 + 19.2 = 51.2\text{ N} \quad (\text{downwards})$$

Calculate the resultant force magnitude:
$$R_P = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2} = \sqrt{25.6^2 + 51.2^2} = \sqrt{655.36 + 2621.44} = \sqrt{3276.8} \approx 57.2433 \approx 57.2\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find horizontal load on pulley:
- Only the slope segment pulls horizontally:
$$X = 32 \times 0.8 = 25.6\text{ N}$$

Find vertical downward load on pulley:
- Both the hanging weight and slope segment pull downwards:
$$Y = 32 + 32(0.6) = 51.2\text{ N}$$

Combine by Pythagoras:
$$R_P = \sqrt{25.6^2 + 51.2^2} = \sqrt{3276.8} \approx 57.2\text{ N}$$
The pulley axle supports a resultant thrust of $57.2\text{ N}$.

hints: Perpendicular to the incline, the horizontal push presses into the slope: $R_A = 80\cos 30^\circ + H\sin 30^\circ = 40\sqrt{3} + 0.5H$.

When $A$ is on the verge of sliding down, friction acts up the slope: $H\cos 30^\circ + T + \mu R_A = 80\sin 30^\circ$.
Substitute $R_A$: $H\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 25 + 0.2(40\sqrt{3} + 0.5H) = 40 \implies 0.9660 H = 15 - 8\sqrt{3} \approx 1.144 \implies H_{\min} \approx 1.18\text{ N}$.

Resolve forces perpendicular to the inclined plane in terms of $H$:
$$\Sigma F_\perp = R_A - m_A g\cos 30^\circ - H\sin 30^\circ = 0$$
$$R_A = 80\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 0.5H = 40\sqrt{3} + 0.5H$$

Identify string tension and parallel forces when block $A$ slips down:
- String tension: $T = m_B g = 2.5(10) = 25\text{ N}$ (acting up the slope).
- Push component: $H\cos 30^\circ$ (acting up the slope).
- Friction force: $F_{\max} = 0.2 R_A$ (acting up the slope).

$$H\cos 30^\circ + 25 + 0.2(40\sqrt{3} + 0.5H) - 40 = 0$$

Calculate the minimum force $H_{\min}$:
$$H_{\min} = \frac{1.1436}{0.966025} \approx 1.1838 \approx 1.18\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find normal reaction with horizontal push:
- Pushing horizontally adds a perpendicular component:
$$R_A = 40\sqrt{3} + 0.5H$$

Set up force balance along slope:
- Downhill gravity ($40\text{ N}$) is opposed by rope tension ($25\text{ N}$), friction, and push:
$$H\cos 30^\circ + 25 + 0.2 R_A = 40\text{ N}$$

Solve for minimum push:
$$H_{\min} = \frac{1.144}{0.966} \approx 1.18\text{ N}$$
A slight horizontal push of $1.18\text{ N}$ prevents block $A$ from sliding downhill.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Capstone Practice 2: Deflected hanging mass with crest pulley reaction

hints: Particle $B$ is in equilibrium under three coplanar forces: downward weight $m_B g = 40\text{ N}$, horizontal pull $Q$, and string tension $T$ inclined at angle $\beta$ to the vertical.
Vertical balance: $T\cos\beta = 40\text{ N}$. Horizontal balance: $T\sin\beta = Q$.
Square and add to eliminate $\beta$: $T^2(\cos^2\beta + \sin^2\beta) = 40^2 + Q^2 \implies T = \sqrt{1600 + Q^2}$.
Divide horizontal by vertical to find the angle relation: $\tan\beta = \frac{Q}{40}$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve forces vertically for particle $B$:
$$\Sigma F_y = T\cos\beta - m_B g = 0 \implies T\cos\beta = 4(10) = 40\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces horizontally for particle $B$:
$$\Sigma F_x = T\sin\beta - Q = 0 \implies T\sin\beta = Q$$

Combine equations by squaring and adding, and taking the ratio:
$$T^2 = (T\cos\beta)^2 + (T\sin\beta)^2 = 40^2 + Q^2 = 1600 + Q^2$$
$$T = \sqrt{1600 + Q^2}, \quad \tan\beta = \frac{Q}{40}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Balance particle $B$ along vertical axis:
$$T\cos\beta = 40\text{ N}$$

Balance particle $B$ along horizontal axis:
$$T\sin\beta = Q$$

Form tension and angle equations:
$$T = \sqrt{1600 + Q^2}, \quad \tan\beta = \frac{Q}{40}$$
The deflection directly controls string tension.

hints: For particle $A$ on the incline: $R_A = 60\cos 30^\circ = 30\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$. Maximum static friction is $F_{A,\max} = 0.4(30\sqrt{3}) = 12\sqrt{3} \approx 20.78\text{ N}$.
Particle $A$ is on the point of slipping UP the slope, so friction acts DOWN the slope.
Maximum tension: $T_{\max} = 60\sin 30^\circ + 12\sqrt{3} = 30 + 20.7846 = 50.7846\text{ N}$.
Equate $T = \sqrt{1600 + Q^2} = 50.7846 \implies Q_{\max} = \sqrt{50.7846^2 - 1600} = \sqrt{979.08} \approx 31.3\text{ N}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate normal reaction and maximum static friction on particle $A$:
$$R_A = m_A g\cos 30^\circ = 60\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = 30\sqrt{3} \approx 51.9615\text{ N}$$
$$F_{A,\max} = \mu R_A = 0.4(30\sqrt{3}) = 12\sqrt{3} \approx 20.7846\text{ N}$$

Determine the maximum tension $T_{\max}$ before particle $A$ slides up the plane:
$$\Sigma F_\parallel = T - m_A g\sin 30^\circ - F_{A,\max} = 0$$
$$T_{\max} = 60(0.5) + 12\sqrt{3} = 30 + 20.7846 = 50.7846\text{ N}$$

Solve for the maximum horizontal deflecting force $Q_{\max}$:
$$T_{\max}^2 = 1600 + Q_{\max}^2 = 50.7846^2 \approx 2579.076$$
$$Q_{\max}^2 = 2579.076 - 1600 = 979.076$$
$$Q_{\max} = \sqrt{979.076} \approx 31.2902 \approx 31.3\text{ N}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Assess particle $A$ threshold:
- Downhill weight is $30\text{ N}$ and friction grip is:
$$F_{\max} = 0.4 \times 30\sqrt{3} = 12\sqrt{3} \approx 20.78\text{ N}$$

Find maximum string tension:
$$T_{\max} = 30 + 20.78 = 50.78\text{ N}$$

Calculate maximum sideways pull on $B$:
$$Q_{\max} = \sqrt{50.78^2 - 40^2} = \sqrt{979.1} \approx 31.3\text{ N}$$
Pulling horizontally with more than $31.3\text{ N}$ drags block $A$ up the slope.
